listings.loreTeaser: It made Dexter Curtis's patented zinc-lined horse-collar pads, which sold nationwide, became apartments after the company left in 1913, and has stood empty…

listings.name: Former Pirate's Park (closed fun park, Flint Township)
listings.summary: A pirate-themed fun park that opened in 1991 with mini golf, go-karts and a 420-foot water slide.
listings.loreTeaser: It closed in 2011 and decayed for years while reopening plans fell through, then was demolished in June 2024.

listings.name: Skillagalee (Ile aux Galets) + Gravelly Shoal Lighthouses (two-light package)
listings.summary: Two Great Lakes lighthouses for less than a starter home.
listings.loreTeaser: One is the 1888 brick tower on Ile aux Galets, the 'island of pebbles' 7 miles off Cross Village; the other is the 1939-41 Art Deco Gravelly Shoal light in…
listings.geo_source: Twisted Deeds map layer (landmark (Nominatim, Ile aux Galets island); Gravelly Shoal light is a second site in Saginaw Bay)

listings.name: Middle Island & Lighthouse (227-acre Lake Huron island)
listings.summary: A 227-acre island in the Thunder Bay shipwreck graveyard, with a 76-foot lighthouse first lit in 1905.
listings.loreTeaser: Volunteer keepers spent decades restoring the station from 1992 and turned its fog-signal building into a remote overnight inn.
listings.geo_source: Twisted Deeds map layer (landmark (Nominatim, Middle Island Light))

listings.name: Farrand Hall (1854 Greek Revival homestead)
listings.summary: A pioneer's 1854 Greek Revival mansion with a 170-year chain of ownership on the record.
listings.loreTeaser: Henry K. Farrand arrived in 1836 and his wife died the year after the house was finished.

listings.name: Former Moline Public Library (1904 Carnegie)
listings.summary: A Neoclassical Carnegie library that opened in 1904 with Ionic columns and five fireplaces.
listings.loreTeaser: It closed as a library in 2009 and stood empty until a music conservatory moved in in 2023.

listings.name: Former Kendallville Carnegie Library
listings.summary: Kendallville's Carnegie library (cornerstone 1913, finished 1914) served the town until 1968.
listings.loreTeaser: It then passed through a law firm, an architecture practice, a vintage shop and an art gallery, and is now going to online auction with a published minimum bid.
